notes: Meeting-scheduling / ICS task. The implementer must (1) parse attendee availability minutes and find the EARLIEST conflict-free slot, emitting a standards-conformant iCalendar event for it, and (2) correctly apply recovery-buffer-after-late-meeting semantics when an occupied meeting ends at/after late_hour, in which case the effective occupied region is extended by buffer_after_late_min before the slot search, and (3) locate a provided per-person schedule producer tool, read its calling convention, and drive it to save one snapshot text file per attendee. hidden_case_generalization=3: the same /app/schedule.py is re-run by the verifier over fresh read-only availability sets (/tests/hidden/*) with distinct windows, durations, buffer sizes and degenerate inputs, and must independently reconstruct the same earliest DTSTART. reasoning_depth=2: the buffer rule changes the earliest slot only when the naive conflict-free choice falls within a recovery buffer (the evening-buffer hidden case forces 23:30 vs a naive 22:30), so an implementer who skips the recovery-buffer extension produces the wrong start. debugging_ambiguity=2: the malformed/overlapping/zero-length availability lines and the >= versus > boundary at exactly late_hour must be handled per the documented rule with no visibility into the hidden sets. dependent_stages=2: earliest-slot derivation feeds the ICS emission and the summary, and the personals are a separate discovery stage. Resource pressure is low, so the total sits in the medium bucket.
